name: Clonbeg Cutaway
blurb: A midland cutaway: eighty years of peat taken by the ton and the narrow-gauge railway left rusting in the heather. Nobody wants it, which is why you can have it. Let the water back and see.

lines: Bare dark peat in long fields, drains running straight to nowhere.
Drains blocked, birch seedlings starting along the edges.
A shallow lake forming, reeds and rushes along its edge.
Wetland, birch scrub, a lake full of birds, and a corncrake somewhere in the grass.

ranger: Cutaway bog, bare as a table. The Board took the peat and left the shape of the hole.
Drains are blocked and birch is starting along the edges. Give it a few winters.
A shallow lake is forming, rushes along its edge. The waders have found it already.
Wetland, birch scrub and a lake full of birds. A corncrake in the meadow, would you believe.
